conclusions.fullWasi: The pinned full Swift/WASI reactor flags and the prior test-only export produce a 5,508,619-byte no-op with 20 initial pages, already 1,314,315 bytes over the unchanged limit. The same-profile scalar is 5,534,860 bytes, 26,241 bytes above the no-op and 3 bytes above the prior 5,534,857-byte measurement. The source preserves the previous scalar parser, limits and count result and adds an explicit empty-input early return. The link map assigns 4,318,673 no-op CODE bytes to libswiftCore.a. Extraction starts from swiftrt.o referencing swift_addNewDSOImage. These are measured closure sizes for the pinned link, not lower bounds on all Swift configurations.
conclusions.embedded: Pinned official Swift 6.3.3 Embedded WASI uses the SDK embedded resources, the same target and reactor model, and the Embedded toolset Swift options. Freestanding controls use the repository saved-draft compiler/linker flags with the same test-only export and no capability objects. Neither profile changes the installed guest ABI. TaskWire probes use the unchanged saved-draft TaskWireReader for StaticString, UInt64.max decimal, base64 state, a flag byte, exact consumption and negatives. Compact no-op, raw input and TaskWire validate in the strict Rust mixer-table-memory-v3 tool. Positive byte cases execute under Node WASI with empty arguments, environment and preopens. Mixer VM invocation covered return 0 on the no-op and TaskWire null-input rejection, not positive host-buffer transfer.
conclusions.scalar: Both unmodified Foundation-free scalar extracts fail Embedded compilation at existential any Error. A private typed-throws adaptation preserves the count probe and maps the typed scanner error into a flat-codec error. It compiles then needs the SDK-shipped Unicode data archive to resolve normalization symbols. The official archive links a 119,642-byte scalar count reactor and a 119,701-byte exact-output companion, both at 3 initial pages. Each passes 22 Node WASI checks, including 6 accepted JSON values, 13 document rejections and 3 pointer/count boundary observations. Exact-output companion verifies canonical bytes for the accepted vectors.
conclusions.strictImport: The protected Embedded WASI allocating array and scalar both import random_get and fail strict Rust VM validation. Disabling stack protection solely for attribution makes the array control import-free and validation pass. The scalar retains the arc4random_buf to getentropy to random_get chain and still fails. No runtime or installed policy was changed, and the diagnostic is no basis for removing protection in production.
conclusions.historicalEditor: GitHub source bytes for the pinned before TaskEditor and after TaskEditorPresentation match the historical corpus Git blobs. Both fail typecheck at import Foundation in both Embedded profiles. The controls cover bytes, numeric wire fields and reduced JSON scalar behavior. This trial supplies no Embedded execution for actor-backed title/responsible edits and submit, asynchronous persistence and completion, V3 revision/identity routing and stale/foreign/wrong-value rejection, cancel pop without persistence, startup/document framing, lock-based V1 cutoff or retirement for the original components. The first import blocker masks further compile checks for those exact files.
conclusions.nextExecutableTest: Build a second bounded typed-throws scalar with collection hashing removed from the guard and flat extractor, using explicit bounded byte-key comparison and retaining the prior duplicate-key and field-key semantics. Keep the existing WASI target and stack protector. Inspect its why-extract map and run strict validation plus the 22-check WASI canonical-byte and rejection fixture. If a standard retained stack-guard import still fails, confirm whether the unchanged installed activation owner already admits that precise import before proceeding. Passing this control would only justify the exact historical editor closure build and separate signed admission/replay with unchanged V1 cutoff, V3 stale/action/cancel and retirement assertions.

scalarSourceRecipe: Read the two source files at sourceRevision. Check the baseline hashes from the supplied scalar receipt. Apply its verified delivered patch only to private copies and verify the patched hashes.
For JSONInputGuard.swift remove import Foundation and remove its Data validation method, retaining validateBytes and scanner.
For FlatEvent.swift concatenate the GuestUIEventCodecErrorV1 enum and the file tail beginning func appendGuestUIJSONStringV1. Exclude both imports and the Data-facing V1 codec.

In TypedGuard.swift replace throws with throws(JSONInputError) in the standalone guard. In TypedFlatEvent.swift replace throws with throws(GuestUIEventCodecErrorV1), add case invalidString(JSONInputError), and wrap the scanner call in do throws(JSONInputError) { return try JSONInputGuard.decodeString(in: bytes, at: &index) } catch { throw .invalidString(error) }. See fixtureSource for the two typed wrappers.
The TaskWire.swift input is the exact current Git blob at tests/integration/fieldlog-saved-draft/guest/TaskWire.swift. Use the runtime harness below for positive inputs.
setupCorrections: Initial shell setup found no verification/local directory and launched no compiler. Created only the ignored owned parent before running the controls.
The first FlatEvent extraction carried through the MixerCore SPI import. The corrected standalone scalar extract drops that import.
The first Embedded WASI command reused the full-SDK resource directory verbatim. Embedded WASI succeeded with the SDK swift resource view, whose embedded directory contains the WASI Swift module.

The initial Unicode result collector looked for ok instead of valid in VM validation JSON. The observed compiler and validator commands closed. The corrected collector reused their outputs, then executed the exact-output companion separately.
